orangeDuplicateDecision.determination: Same canonical botanical taxon (sweet orange). Catalog notation is inconsistent: orange uses Citrus sinensis; sweet-orange uses Citrus × sinensis. Hybrid marker × is matching-only, not a distinct taxon.
orangeDuplicateDecision.classB: not proven as a distinct product taxon; common-name split (Orange Tree vs Sweet orange) is not botanical distinctness
orangeDuplicateDecision.classC: taxonomic notation inconsistency (hybrid marker × / x omitted)
orangeDuplicateDecision.classD: notation is explained; remaining product-alias question is held, not merged

botanicalTaxonIdProposal.note: canonicalSlug is a product/common-name identity. It is not necessarily a unique botanical taxon. Size evidence should attach to botanicalTaxonId.

fields.canonicalPlantAliases: canonicalSlug list that resolve to this taxon

pilotConflictClassification.differingRanges: FEIS generally 30–55 m tall vs SelecTree maximum landscape height 80 ft (~24.4 m)
pilotConflictClassification.differingContext: Ecological/naturalized stature versus landscape selection maxima. Do not downscale the FEIS botanical range because home gardens cannot accommodate it. Do not average.
pilotConflictClassification.reason: FEIS NATURAL_MATURE typical range vs SelecTree landscape maxima. Already captured as different scenarios.

pilotConflictClassification.differingRanges: UF/IFAS height 40–60 ft vs NCSU 40–70 ft; spread both 3–6 ft
pilotConflictClassification.differingContext: Same columnar landscape form; height maxima differ. Do not average. Narrow spread is architecture, not error.
pilotConflictClassification.reason: Same LANDSCAPE_MATURE columnar scenario; height maxima 60 vs 70 ft disagree. Spread agrees. Do not average.

pilotConflictClassification.differingRanges: about 30 ft unpruned vs 30–40 ft seedling standard
pilotConflictClassification.differingContext: Both are seedling/standard class. Do not average. Spread given only by the about-30-ft record.
pilotConflictClassification.reason: Both seedling/standard class. One record is approximate “about 30 ft”; the other is a 30–40 ft range. Source definition, not a second taxon.

pilotConflictClassification.differingRanges: Morton 15–25 ft tall × 15–35 ft wide vs Virginia 12–25 ft tall × 10–25 ft wide, both depending on cultivar
pilotConflictClassification.differingContext: Cultivar variability is the shared explanation. Do not average. Do not invent cultivar records.
pilotConflictClassification.reason: Both sources state cultivar-dependent stature. Range mismatch is cultivar variability, not a second species.
